prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1335; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's policyholder following a sideswipe that occurred while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant reports a wrist fracture and is represented by counsel, who has requested all future contact be routed through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. No concerns were identified regarding the policy status.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver, all of whom confirm the collision happened as the claimant described. Scene photographs were also received and are consistent with the account given.

Entry 4: Inspected the insured vehicle. The damage to the driver side panels matches the described impact pattern. A few older scratches are visible in the same area and may predate this loss; these have been noted separately for the file.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's counsel, who provided the medical records for the wrist fracture. The injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and the claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far.

Entry 6: Medical file shows treatment followed a usual course, with care tapering off as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the records received to date.

Entry 7: Reviewed the claimant's seating position with the available information. It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting at the moment of impact, and this will be clarified in a follow-up interview.

Entry 8: Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage occurred before the coverage start date. Requested the prior repair history to close out the question of the older scratches.

Entry 9: File reviewed and remains open pending the follow-up interview on seating position and receipt of the prior repair history. Injury and liability information to date are consistent with the reported facts.
